runs.summary: 4 new podcast recommendations for week of 2026-10-08 (Excess Returns, Interconnects, The Proof, The Creative Penn)
runs.content:
## Week of 2026-10-08

### Excess Returns
**Hosts:** Jack Forehand, Justin Carbonneau (Validea) and Matt Zeigler
**Why for Fred:** Fred has listened to [[podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-rich-pzena]] and [[podcast-dividend-talk-ep305-cyclical-stocks]], so he is interested in how value and quality investing actually hold up in practice. Excess Returns comes from a quant-factor shop (Validea runs guru-based screening models) and tests value, momentum and quality factors against the data instead of telling stories about them. That suits someone who runs his own screens and paper-trading strategies. The guest list is strong across value managers and macro strategists, and the shows on bond yields pick up where [[podcast-odd-lots-bond-yields-surge]] and Prof G's "bonds are warning" episode left off.
**Format:** Long-form interview plus panel episodes, several a week, ~60–90 min
**Sample episode to start with:** "The 10-Year Hit a 24-Year High. Nobody Is Buying Puts." (Oct 3, 2026), with Andy Constan, Brent Kochuba and Eric Pachman, which ties bond yields to options positioning. Or the Michael Baron (Baron Capital) episode on long-horizon compounders (Oct 1, 2026).
**Links:** [Spotify for Creators](https://podcasters.spotify.com/pod/show/excess-returns) · [Pocket Casts](https://pocketcasts.com/podcast/excess-returns/e3eb2590-f8f0-0137-b597-0acc26574db2)

---

### Interconnects
**Host:** Nathan Lambert (post-training lead at Ai2, author of the *Interconnects* newsletter)
**Why for Fred:** Fred's AI listening ([[podcast-dwarkesh-compute-prices-10x]], [[podcast-dwarkesh-ais-learning-on-the-job]]) is mostly about where capability and inference economics are going. Lambert is a working researcher who trains open models, so he covers the open-vs-closed model balance, recursive self-improvement claims and the US–China gap from inside the field rather than as a commentator. The previously suggested AI shows (Latent Space, No Priors, Cognitive Revolution, Training Data) are mostly about builders and startups. Interconnects is closer to Dwarkesh's technical-but-sceptical tone, and its shorter "audio essays" make a good complement.
**Format:** Mix of audio essays (~15–25 min) and long-form researcher interviews (~60–90 min), roughly weekly
**Sample episode to start with:** "Debating RSI, the US-China Gap, and Jaggedness with JS Denain of Epoch AI" (Sept 22, 2026). Or the short essay "Why I still haven't bought into true RSI" (Sept 19, 2026).
**Links:** [interconnects.ai](https://www.interconnects.ai/) · [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/interconnects/id1719552353)

---

### The Proof with Simon Hill
**Host:** Simon Hill (MSc nutrition, physiotherapist)
**Why for Fred:** It is built around the same "live better for longer" question as Fred's longevity-for-men-at-50 interest. Hill's guests are mostly academic clinicians and researchers, not influencers, and he spends a lot of time on how good the evidence actually is. The recent run covers bone health and falls, liver disease, and heart-health strategies. Those are the practical midlife risks that the previously suggested Attia/FoundMyFitness/ZOE shows mention less often. It follows naturally from Fred's interest in the [[podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-creatine-is-the-fat-loss-secret-doctors-dont-tell-you]] episode.
**Format:** Long-form interview, weekly, ~60–90 min
**Sample episode to start with:** "Bone Health, Falls, Medications & Healthy Longevity" with Dr Deborah Kado, Stanford geriatrician (Aug 31, 2026)
**Links:** [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-proof-with-simon-hill/id1367773989) · [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/0WuG4lkB2lIGpo8WgdBeOM)

---

### The Creative Penn Podcast For Writers
**Host:** Joanna Penn (UK indie author of 40+ books, running the show since 2009)
**Why for Fred:** Lightfin and The Optimised Jungle are self-driven creative projects with no publisher behind them, and Fred works on both alongside heavy AI use. Penn is the best-known voice on exactly that combination: indie publishing plus AI-assisted creative work. The craft shows already suggested (Writing Excuses, Scriptnotes, Sound School) teach story and audio technique. Creative Penn covers what comes after: getting the work published, found and turned into a living, plus where to draw the line with AI.
**Format:** Long-form interview, weekly, ~45–60 min
**Sample episode to start with:** "What Machines Can't Replace: Why AI Makes Us More Human" with Anna McPhee (Sept 9, 2026). Or "Book Marketing, AI Book Discoverability, And Resilience" with Ricardo Fayet (Aug 19, 2026).
**Links:** [thecreativepenn.com/podcasts](https://www.thecreativepenn.com/podcasts/)

Week of 2026-10-01

#Conversations with Tyler
Host: Tyler Cowen (economist, George Mason University; Marginal Revolution)
Why for Fred: Fred listens to podcast-dwarkesh-podcast a lot, and the podcast-dwarkesh-alex-imas-phil-trammell-what-remains-scarce-after-agi episode is the economist-on-AI angle he keeps returning to. Cowen is a regular Dwarkesh guest and the economist that show most often draws on. His own interviews are among the densest long-form conversations available. His 2026 book *Messy Jobs* argues that AI won't cause mass unemployment because it makes jobs messier, which is exactly the "AI impact on work" question in Fred's wiki. Unlike the AI shows already suggested (No Priors, Latent Space, Training Data, Cognitive Revolution, Big Technology), Cowen covers economics, culture and history as well as AI.
Format: Long-form interview, roughly fortnightly, ~60–90 min. Unusually fast-paced with no small talk.
Sample episode to start with: The Luis Garicano episodes (July 28 and August 27, 2026). They cover *Messy Jobs*, why AI won't cause mass unemployment, and whether AI eases debt burdens or causes stagflation.
Links: https://conversationswithtyler.com/ · https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/conversations-with-tyler/id983795625

#Merryn Talks Money
Host: Merryn Somerset Webb (Bloomberg senior columnist, ex-editor of MoneyWeek)
Why for Fred: Almost every finance show on Fred's list or in past suggestions is US-centric. The only European-focused ones are podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet and Dividend Talk. Somerset Webb is a UK value-leaning sceptic who gives the European/UK investor's view of the same macro questions Fred has been hearing from podcast-odd-lots-bond-yields-surge and Prof G Markets: bond yields, AI-capex bubble risk, gold. She also covers UK-specific practical topics like inheritance tax and ISAs. It fits his European value-investing orientation better than another US markets show would.
Format: Interview plus a markets-wrap episode, about twice weekly, ~30–45 min
Sample episode to start with: "Stocks That Could Beat an AI Bust" (Sept 24, 2026). It ties straight into the AI-bubble worries in his recent Prof G and Invest Like the Best (Gavin Baker) episodes.
Links: https://www.bloomberg.com/merryn-talks-money-podcast · https://music.amazon.com/podcasts/d2523363-a1eb-4c7e-8875-7b05f26ac13c/merryn-talks-money

#ZOE Science & Nutrition
Hosts: Jonathan Wolf with Prof Tim Spector (King's College London), Prof Sarah Berry and Dr Federica Amati
Why for Fred: The longevity shows already suggested (Peter Attia, FoundMyFitness, Dementia Matters, High Intensity Health) are mostly American and clinician-led. ZOE is UK-based and built around the ZOE PREDICT nutrition studies, the largest of their kind. The 2026 episodes keep coming back to dementia prevention, one of his core health interests. The podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-creatine-is-the-fat-loss-secret-doctors-dont-tell-you episode showed he responds to practical, evidence-based nutrition content, and ZOE does that every week.
Format: Interview, weekly, ~45–60 min, with short "recap" episodes in between
Sample episode to start with: "The 6 rules you need for a long, healthy life and how to cut your risk of dementia, heart disease and cancer" with Dr Ezekiel Emanuel (July 16, 2026). Alternatively, the Prof Ed Bullmore episode on inflammation and the brain (June 11, 2026).
Links: https://zoe.com/learn/podcast-exploring-dementia · https://www.audible.co.uk/podcast/ZOE-Science-Nutrition/B09T4QG5G9

#Circle Round
Producer: WBUR Boston (Rebecca Sheir, host/co-creator)
Why for Fred: This one is for craft rather than personal listening. Lightfin is a children's audio project, and Circle Round is arguably the best-produced children's audio drama around. It turns folktales from around the world into 15–25 minute radio plays with original music, a full cast and sound design, for "ages 3–103." Writing Excuses, Scriptnotes and Sound School (all previously suggested) teach story craft and audio production in the abstract; Circle Round shows the finished product, in the same format and for the same audience as Lightfin. The new interactive spin-off in its feed, *The Midnight Rebellion*, ends each episode with a choice for the listener, a structural idea worth studying.
Format: Narrative audio drama, weekly, ~15–25 min
Sample episode to start with: "The Hiding Place" (encore, Sept 29, 2026). Also try the first episode of *The Midnight Rebellion* to hear the interactive-choice format.
Links: https://www.wbur.org/podcasts/circleround · https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/circle-round/id1246443751
